facts.fact_text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in the city of Malatya.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, a group comprising hundreds of police officers formed a cordon around the crowd.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, was a spokesperson for the Women's Democratic Platform.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicants were exercising their constitutional right.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.
Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
Ill-treatment of the detained women continued in the police vehicles after their arrest on 8 March 2005.
Male police officers started squeezing the arms and legs of the detained women inside the police vehicles.
The detained women told the police officers that the police officers had no right to behave as they were behaving.
The detained women asked for female police officers to accompany them in the police vehicles.
When the detained women told the police officers they had no right to behave as they were and asked for female police officers, the detained women were sworn at by the police officers.
The episode of ill-treatment in the police vehicles lasted for approximately twenty minutes.
The four arrested applicants were taken to a police station on 8 March 2005.
After being taken to a police station, the four arrested applicants were subsequently taken to the Forensic Medicine Institute for a medical examination on 8 March 2005.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the four applicants who had been hit by police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the injuries sustained by the four applicants rendered them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.
Later on 8 March 2005, the four arrested applicants were released from police custody.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.
According to the Government's submissions, a police chief warned the participants on 8 March 2005 that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief told the participants that they could leave their placards — which were too large — and walk on the pavement, and that the placards would be returned to them later.
According to the Government's submissions, the force used to put the persons into the police vehicles could not be considered disproportionate.
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrations at the International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya on 8 March 2005 hindered the flow of traffic.
According to the Government's submissions, a group of police officers tried to convince the demonstrators to disperse on 8 March 2005.
According to the Government's submissions, police officers requested the demonstrators to hold their demonstrations without impeding the circulation of traffic on 8 March 2005.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief made several unsuccessful attempts to tell the participants that the manner in which they were conducting their demonstration was unlawful because they were impeding the flow of traffic.
According to the Government's submissions, the group of demonstrators insisted on blocking the street and continued with their demonstration on 8 March 2005.
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrators shouted slogans and continued to protest despite police officers' warnings and efforts on 8 March 2005.
According to the Government's submissions, ten to fifteen police officers formed a cordon around the participants who had been giving orders to the rest of the demonstrators on 8 March 2005.
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrators inside the police cordon continued to protest, saying that they would not end the illegal demonstration even if they were arrested.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
Ill-treatment of the detained women continued in the police vehicles after their arrest on 8 March 2005.
Male police officers started squeezing the arms and legs of the detained women inside the police vehicles.
The detained women told the police officers that the police officers had no right to behave as they were behaving.
The detained women asked for female police officers to accompany them in the police vehicles.
When the detained women told the police officers they had no right to behave as they were and asked for female police officers, the detained women were sworn at by the police officers.
The episode of ill-treatment in the police vehicles lasted for approximately twenty minutes.
According to the Government's submissions, the force used to put the persons into the police vehicles could not be considered disproportionate.
A police chief told the Malatya prosecutor that the force used by the police on 8 March 2005 had been proportionate.
Four of the police officers told the Malatya prosecutor that the police officers had had to use force on 8 March 2005, as a result of which the demonstrators might have suffered minor injuries.
In his report of 18 April 2005, the Malatya prosecutor expressed the opinion that the use of force by the police officers on 8 March 2005 had not been excessive.
